We have 2 homes: both in zone 8. Near the coast of the Pacific. Will your milkweed seeds grow here, or will your seed bombs work as well? I also worry about native plants. It is a non-native and invasive plant brought over from Europe years ago. How would I find out if any of the seeds in your seed bombs would be invasive to my two zip code areas in California and Oregon?

 Thank you!

messages.text:
Hi Shelly,

Great questions, and yes, our milkweed seeds and seed bombs will grow well in zone 8 on both the Pacific coast of California and Oregon.

On the native/invasive concern: this is a really thoughtful question, and the honest answer is that none of the milkweed species we sell are foreign invasives like Scotchbroom. They're all native to North America. That said, a few species like Common milkweed (Asclepias syriaca) are native to eastern and central North America and not naturally found on the Pacific coast, so while they won't behave like Scotchbroom (which has no natural controls out west), you'd likely prefer species that are truly local to your region.

For California and Oregon specifically, Narrowleaf milkweed (Asclepias fascicularis) and Showy milkweed (Asclepias speciosa) are both native to the Pacific coast and the western US, those would be my top picks for your two properties. You can see what we currently have here: https://lasclay.com/en/products/milkweed-seeds

For extra peace of mind on what's considered native to your exact zip codes, the Calflora database (calflora.org) for California and the Oregon Flora Project are great free resources to cross-reference.

If you'd like a second opinion on species before ordering, just send me a note and I'll help you pick.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
